title: Modeling the Rate of Change in Irrigation Water Quality Between Spring and Winter in Coastal Wells in the Municipality of Guasave, Sinaloa, Mexico
content: The goal of this study is to model the rate of change between spring and winter in groundwater quality for irrigation in coastal wells in the municipality of Guasave, Sinaloa, Mexico. In 58 well-water samples (29 sampled in spring and 29 in winter), the following parameters were measured: pH, electrical conductivity (E.C.), total dissolved solids, temperature, salinity, static water level, Na+, Ca2+, Mg2+, K+, Cl–, SO42–, CO32–, and HCO3–. The original sodium adsorption ratio (SARor), corrected (SARco), and adjusted (SARad) were calculated. For spring and winter and using Pearson and Spearman (Sr) coefficients, ordinary and repeated measures correlations were calculated. To identify differences between seasons, paired tests and Piper diagrams were used. The rate of quality change was modeled using multiple non-linear regressions. All models were rigorously validated. For the quality change rate, three predictive quadratic polynomial models were obtained. These three models presented the following significant values for Sr: 0.653 (E.C. vs. SARor), 0.575 (E.C. vs. SARco), and 0.470 (E.C. vs. SARad). Observed and predicted quality were numerically classified based on E.C. vs. SARor, SARco, and SARad. The information from these models can be applied to prevent soil contamination caused by irrigation with saline and sodic water, potentially boosting agricultural yields in ‘‘the agricultural heart of Mexico.’’
